chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Abd al-A'la, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever travels to this House as a pilgrim or one performing Umrah, free from arrogance, will return from his sins as he was on the day his mother gave birth to him.'
Then whoever hastens off in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him, (this is) the one who fears.

I said, 'What is arrogance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The greatest of arrogance is contempt for the people and foolishness regarding the truth.' I said, 'What is contempt for the people and foolishness regarding the truth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He disregards the truth and slanders its people; and whoever does that, disputes with Allah regarding His cloak.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of arrogance (al-kibr) in Shia hadith and how does it affect Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the spiritual efficacy of Hajj to the purification of the ego, specifically defining 'al-kibr' (arrogance) not merely as pride, but as the active rejection of truth and disparagement of its adherents. This interpretation aligns with the Shia exegetical tradition where 'disputing with Allah’s cloak' signifies a direct challenge to divine authority and grace, emphasizing that ritual correctness must be accompanied by moral humility to achieve the promised state of sinlessness.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali in Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abdul A’ala who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The one who travels to this House (Kabah) as a pilgrim, or performs Umra free from arrogance, would return from his sins to as he was on the day his mother gave him birth’.
Then heasws recited [2:203] then whoever hastens off in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him, (this is) the one who fears’.

I said, ‘What is the arrogance?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The greatest of all arrogant ones are the most contemptible of the people and the most foolish of the people’. I said, ‘Who are the most contemptible of the people and the most foolish of the people?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who is ignorant of the Truth, and he slanders against his family; and the one who does that, would have disputed with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with his cloak’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from ‘Abd al-‘ Ala’ who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘My father would say, “One who decides to perform Hajj or ‘Umrah free of al-Kibr (arrogance) returns, in matters of sins, as the day his mother gave birth to him.’”
He (the Imam) then read this, ‘On one who hastens during the two days, there is no sin, and on one who delays, there is no sin.’ [2:199]

I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What is al-Kibr?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “The greatest al-Kibr is ghamd and Safah of the creatures.’” I then asked, ‘What is ghamd and safah of creatures?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is ignoring the truth, and falsifying the people of truth. Whoever does this has quarreled with Allah about His gown.’”
